transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora. I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. Firstly, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening about 1 week after your surgery. However, you should avoid any heavy lifting or strenuous exercise for a full month after surgery.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the info! I was wondering when I can start using my eye gel for dry eyes again.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question! It's safe to continue using your eye gel for dry eyes. If you were using it before your operation, you can keep using it now, unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

If you're running low on it, your GP should be able to provide more for you.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That’s helpful, thank you! I'm finding that I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check it further. Do you have any redness or pain along with the light sensitivity?

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, there's no pain or redness, just sensitivity. I have one last question: should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question, but I'd need to know how long it's been since your surgery to give you the best answer. 

It's common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time. However, if your vision is still quite blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

How long ago was your surgery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text:
My surgery was about two weeks ago. I guess it's not too blurry, just not as clear as I'd hoped. 

Thank you for all your help, Dora. I don't have any more questions at the moment!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
You're welcome! At two weeks, some mild blurriness can still be normal as your eyes continue to settle. It should keep improving over time.

Just to confirm - have all your questions about your surgery and recovery been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, you've answered everything I was curious about. Thanks again for your assistance!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help. Take care, and remember to wear those sunglasses outside!
